subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core admin-scoped shell-to-Control-UI notification contract, fold this request into broader WebUI notification architecture, or reject direct core UI interruption in favor of plugin/external paths?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose the security boundary, payload policy, rate-limit behavior, and UI interruption model for a new shell-originated admin broadcast surface.

options.title: Design Core Notify Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical shell-facing feature and require an explicit Gateway RPC/event, CLI, UI, and security design before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broader UI Notifications
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20237 own the visible notification architecture and close this only after that tracker explicitly includes the admin CLI broadcast contract.

options.title: Prefer Plugin Or External Delivery
options.body: Reject a first-class core command and document the supported plugin, Web Push, channel, or OS-notification path for third-party alerts.

recommendation.title: Design Core Notify Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical shell-facing feature and require an explicit Gateway RPC/event, CLI, UI, and security design before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history points to this person across the central CLI, Gateway, and Control UI files that would need a coordinated security/product decision.
